_comment: #475. `neighborhoods` is informational - BuildingTemplateLibraryImporter reads it for one log
line and nothing matches against it. It now lists exactly the neighborhoods some template
admits, spelled as python/data/sf_analysis_neighborhoods.geojson spells them: the slashes in
"Sunset/Parkside" and the whole of "South of Market" are the match key the bake passes
through verbatim. The previous list carried "Sunset", which is not a neighborhood in that
geojson at all (only "Inner Sunset" and "Sunset/Parkside" are) - dropped.
`districtTemplateWeights` is load-bearing (#343). Two templates now admit the same
neighborhood on purpose - a shopfront cannot share floor 0 with a garage and a door, and the
schema has no way to say 'these two placements are mutually exclusive' inside one template -
so the split has to happen at template selection. Without weights TryMatch's tie-break is
uniform and every second building in the Victorian belt would be a shop.
Caveat: NeighborhoodTemplateWeights.WeightFor treats an authored 0 as 'unset' and falls back
to weight 1, so a weight cannot exclude a template. `trivial_window` (the bundled MVP sample,
compatibility.neighborhoods empty = admits every building in the city) therefore still draws
1 share everywhere; the weights below cut it from ~1 building in 2 to ~1 in 14.
